newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts comments on Fortis nine-month results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comments on Fortis nine-month results.

text.p: AMSTERDAM, Netherlands, Nov 28 - Dutch-Belgian financial services group Fortis reported a net profit of 554 million ecus for the first nine months of 1996, up from 469 million a year earlier.

"The general impression is positive, good figures. It was slightly better than my expectations, especially in banking. Also, unrealised capital gains were better than I expected. There was a surprisingly good increase in life insurance premiums, up almost 18 percent in the third quarter.
"My full year forecast might go up a few cents (per share) but it won't be a very drastic revision."

"They were in line with what I had expected. I had expected 590 million (guilders from Fortis Amev, which reported 605 million), so they were slightly higher but that was mostly in lines like financial transaction income. There were no real surprises. Life insurance was slightly better than expected. I was a little bit surprised that they made a provision in the accident and health insurance in the Netherlands.

"Previously we always looked for America to give problems on accident and health, but it's rather small amount, maybe 20 million ecus -- in the whole of Fortis, that isn't much. (Fortis' forecast of 1996 net profit rising 12-15 percent) looks fine to me. I was looking for earnings per share of around 4.32 guilders. That's pretty much in line with what they've given us." This (result) confirms my positive stance. Through the acquisition of (Dutch merchant bank) MeesPierson...I think that this kind of growth can be continued in 1997 and in 1998 as well, that's why I have it at a strong buy."

TON GIETMAN, VAN MEER JAMES CAPEL "They said at the interims they expected banking to show clearly lower profits in the second half because last year was very good, but that didn't happen in the third quarter."

"It seems life insurance is better than I expected. Overall (the result) is slightly better. Quite a lot of that I can understand. The value differences are a bit of a guess. Banking was slightly better than I expected."
